messages:
Maria: Heads-up — overnight spike of NVIDIA Xid errors in us-east-1 GPU pool. Noticed Xid 79 and 31 mostly, a few 48s. Started ~02:10 UTC and persisted in waves until ~03:20. About 12 nodes touched.
Alex: Confirmed. Alert from infra-bot showed multiple nodes with repeated Xid 79. Correlation looks strong with long-sequence generative jobs (context > 4k tokens) and high per-GPU batch concurrency.
infra-bot: [ALERT] gpu-xid-error: cluster=us-east-1-gpupool count=14 codes={79:8,31:4,48:2} window=1h severity=warning
Jamal: Pushed a quick Prometheus query — shows bump around 02:05. Query I ran: `sum(increase(gpu_xid_total[1h])) by (xid_code)` -> matches infra-bot.
Alex: Also pulled dmesg from one impacted node (gpu-ue1-52). Snippet: ```
[ 1453.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=24351, GPU=0
[ 1453.123500] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=24351, GPU=1
[ 1453.124000] NVRM: GPU fault detected: reason=ECC_UNCORRECTABLE, info=0x7
```
Maria: Interesting — ECC_unable/unrecoverable on one of them. But many nodes show 79 without clear ECC logs. Could be driver/firmware coupling with workload pattern.
Leo: Oncall is cordoning the most-hit nodes so they stop receiving new tasks. I'll start draining gpus: `gcloud compute instances update gpu-ue1-52 --no-scheduling` and `k8s: kubectl drain node/gpu-ue1-52 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
Maria: Thanks. Which nodes are highest? Jamal, can you paste list?
Jamal: Top offenders from last 3 hours: gpu-ue1-52, gpu-ue1-53, gpu-ue1-61, gpu-ue1-64. Frequencies: 52(5), 53(4), 61(3), 64(2).
Alex: Workload side — those GPUs were running high-concurrency gen jobs from the parallax tenant and our internal loadtests with batch_size=16 and sequence length trimmed to 6k in some runs.
Maria: Quick mitigation: reduce concurrency/batch for gen jobs routed to us-east-1-gpupool and send longer jobs to dedicated-dyno (lower concurrency, isolated). Also add fallback route to quantized model variant (smaller memory) when node failure rate > threshold.
Jamal: I put together a Splunk query to correlate with job IDs: `index=gpu_logs "Xid (PCI" | stats count by xid_code, job_id, node` — found repeated job_id 0x9a3b that hit 3 nodes.
infra-bot: [ACTION] Created incident INC-2123 and attached basic diagnostics.
Leo: I'm starting hardware checks on 52/53. Quick `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` shows a handful of ECC errors on 52 but not catastrophic: ```
GPU 0 ECC errors: single-bit=120, double-bit=3
GPU 1 ECC errors: single-bit=78, double-bit=0
```
Maria: double-bit count is small but present — could explain some Xid 31 cases. For Xid 79, sometimes driver kernel panic or watchdog. Are we on stable driver?
Alex: We're on driver branch 525.85; suggested vendor patch is 525.89 that addresses a scheduler corner-case. Jamal: can we test a rolling upgrade on a small slice?
Jamal: I spun up a canary with driver 525.89 on two nodes in staging. No Xid reproduction after targeted load (simulated parallax jobs). I'll start a controlled upgrade on two prod nodes for tonight off-peak.
Maria: Good. Meanwhile ops decision: mark 52/53 as drain-and-retire if further Xid 79s appear after driver update. Open RMA with vendor for potentially flaky HBM2 on those cards.
Alex: For immediate runtime protection: 1) throttle per-GPU concurrency (16->8), 2) enable prefix-KV cache to reduce long seq stress, 3) route >4k token requests to dedicated instances with isolated capacity. I can push a routing rule change in the router config.
Leo: Will do cordon+drain, and place nodes in maintenance in compute console. Jamal: please add the exact node ids to INC-2123 and link RMA ticket.
Jamal: Done — INC-2123 updated; RMA request RMA-874 attached.
Maria: Cost note — routing long-seq jobs to dedicated will increase short-term cost by ~12% for the traffic slice but avoids 3x perf degradation on retries. Put that in the incident summary so finance sees the tradeoff.
Alex: Also adding a short-term autoscale lift on dedicated pool to accept spillover (duration: 6 hrs) to avoid request backpressure.
infra-bot: [CHECKLIST] triage steps: cordon nodes, collect full dmesg+perf, driver canary, reduce batch/concurrency, open RMA, route fallbacks.
Leo: Small ask — can we capture a full pmon trace next time? Add `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` for 10m during the next noisy window. Jamal: scheduled via cron on suspect nodes for 03:00-04:00 UTC daily until fix.
Maria: Follow-ups: Alex to deploy routing rule; Jamal to run driver canary and update INF ticket; Leo to coordinate hardware RMA; SRE-oncall to observe for 12 hrs. Assignments in INC-2123.
sre-oncall: I'll monitor and escalate if error rates don't drop after the driver canary. If Xid 79 persists post-driver, we treat as hardware replacement priority. :triage: 
Alex: One more debugging snippet for future correlation — collect `/proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/ecc_errors` and `dmesg | grep -i Xid` and store with job ids. I'll add to the diagnostic script.
Maria: Thanks team. We'll reconvene in 2 hours or earlier if more noise. :thumbsup:
